name: US jobless claims
summary: US jobless claims 4-week average about 195k, at its 52-week low; 189,000 new claims in the week to 31 Oct
state: Initial US jobless claims were 189,000 in the week to 31 Oct, reported on 5 Nov, keeping the four-week average at about 194,750, its 52-week low and far below the 15% Watch line (Department of Labor via FRED; CNFin). Continuing claims were 1.718m in the week to 24 Oct (CNFin).
for_you: Low claims mean few US layoffs on the latest data. The measure tends to rise early in a downturn, so it is one of the first places weakness would appear.
rubric_hit: 4-week average 0% above its 52-week low, under the 15% Watch line

sources.title: CNFin — US initial jobless claims, week ending 31 Oct

why: Weekly claims are the earliest hard data on US layoffs; a sustained rise usually comes before the unemployment rate turns.
drivers: Layoffs, hiring freezes, federal job cuts, storms, strikes and seasonal quirks.

rubric.normal: The 4-week average of initial claims is less than 15% above its 52-week low.
